coverage_note: Fourth Chapter §§ 24-25 (retention as a transcendence within the phenomenological attitude) and Sixth Chapter § 37 (the temporal principle of the unity of the stream). The 20 other sections with term hits, among them §§ 2 and 8 on the spatio-temporal environment, are not extracted.

units.claim: The demand for nothing but the instantaneous now is said to annihilate its own object, since the now cannot be caught and registered without already being past.
units.quote: Carried to the limit, the demand for nothing-but-the-instantaneous-now annihilates its own object, since the very now cannot be caught and registered without already being past.

units.claim: The reduced perception taken as the enduring lived-experience it is counts as absolutely given, and shrinking it to a durationless instant is called a destruction rather than a heightening of evidence.
units.quote: The reduced perception, taken purely as the enduring lived-experience it is, is the bedrock of indubitable givenness — and the attempt to shrink it to a durationless instant is not a heightening but a *destruction* of evidence.

units.claim: A footnote is reported to set out the presupposed temporal structure: a flowing point of originary self-presence with a retentional horizon of the just-past and a protentional future-horizon.
units.quote: the perception has a *flowing point of originary self-presence* and, beyond it, a *horizon of "retentional" givenness* as just-past, and on the other side an *immediate future-horizon of protentional givenness*

units.claim: The now is called the eternally fleeing boundary-point between past and future, which could not even be asserted to be such if retention were switched off.
units.quote: The now is the *eternally fleeing boundary-point* between past and future — and even *that* it is this could not be asserted if we wanted to switch off *retention*.

units.claim: A transcendence within the phenomenological attitude is admitted: not only retention but what it is retention of, every now of retention being retention of a just-having-been that is given.
units.quote: *Therewith we have admitted a "transcendence" within the phenomenological attitude*: insofar as we admit not only the retention *itself* as phenomenological being, but *also that of which it is retention*.

units.claim: Mistrusting retentional givenness is said to mean absolute skepticism, since that evidence is presupposed in empirical perception too.
units.quote: to *mistrust* such givenness would mean throwing ourselves into the arms of *absolute skepticism*; for such *retentional evidence* is presupposed *also in empirical perception*

units.claim: Every cogitatio is said to be surrounded by a temporal halo that must always be there and, where indeterminate, is determinable rather than freely variable.
units.quote: But it is *absolutely certain* that such a *temporal halo* (*zeitlicher Hof*) is *always there and must be there*, and that, where it is indeterminate, it is *not arbitrarily and freely variable but determinable*.

units.claim: Two experiences joining into one synthetic consciousness join into one experience, to which belongs a time-unity of the experienced, and this is named the single principle constructing the unity of the stream.
units.quote: Two experiences that join *at all* into the unity of a synthetic consciousness spanning them join therein into the unity of *one experience*; and to the unity of one experience there belongs, again, a *time-unity of the experienced*.

units.claim: The unity of the ego is said to be nothing but the lawful synthesizability of its cogitationes into one time, not a substantial pole behind them.
units.quote: The unity of the ego, phenomenologically construed, is thus *nothing but* the lawful synthesizability of its *cogitationes* into one time — not a substantial pole behind them, but the form of their possible temporal interconnection.
